transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-20 10:00am PT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Mikael Andersson (QuantaBank - Head of ML), Renee Cho (QuantaBank - Platform), Diego Ramos (QuantaBank - Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on model selection tradeoffs and version unpinning drill. Reviewed recent latency/cost numbers from the sandbox run, discussed fallback modes and safety net matrix, agreed to run a tabletop unpinning dry-run next week. Security asked for KMS key flow and audit log snippet. Several small transcription/term errors in real-time notes.

Topics covered:
- Recent benchmark highlights (latency by model variant)
- Pin/lock policy and emergency unpinning path
- Fallback sequencing: region->model-variant->dedicated burst
- Safety/regulatory constraints (data residency, KMS)
- Next steps and owners

Action items reviewed at end (see metadata list above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's kick off. quick agenda — a couple minutes on the numbers priya has, then deep on the unpinning/escape plan, and wrap with security asks.
[00:18] Mikael: cool yeah thanks jordan. we're trying not to eat up too much of your time today.
[00:22] Priya: alright i'll share my screen in a sec, but high-level — sandbox run yesterday, we ran the three candidate variants you recommended: rwd-3b-int8, rwd-7b-q4, and rwd-7b-8k. latency median for our golden prompts, small chat flow, was 85ms for 3b, 180ms for 7b-q4, and 240ms for 7b-8k. token cost delta lines up roughly with what you published, 3b about 0.6x of 7b-q4.
[00:45] Diego: sorry priya, when you say 240ms that's p50 or p95?
[00:48] Priya: p50. p95 stretches to 540ms on 7b-8k for that multi-turn prompt, likely due to KV cache rebuilds on our pattern.
[01:02] Renee: kv cache — i'm not sure we saw that in our infra notes, could be the way our session affinity times out.
[01:08] Priya: yeah, on Redwood's side the KV/kv cache timeout is configurable; i ran with conservative settings to match your session length.
[01:15] Jordan: and just to calibrate - the reason we surfaced the three is cost/latency tradeoff. 3b is cheapest/fastest but has occasional quality drops on long-context instructions. 7b variants hold context better but cost more.
[01:30] Mikael: for us top-line is accuracy on compliance classification tasks, so a false negative is bad. we prefer a small latency increase if quality is stable.
[01:39] Priya: understood, which pushes us to favor 7b-q4 with a fallback to 3b for low-cost non-sensitive workloads, and a soft fallback route to 7b-8k only when the context window demands it.
[01:52] Diego: how do we picture the fallback sequence? region first, model second, or model then region?
[01:58] Jordan: good question. our recommended policy for your SLAs: 1) model variant fallback within same region (i.e., 7b-q4 -> 3b), 2) if capacity constrained then route to another region in the same legal boundary, 3) as a last resort use dedicated burst or queued degraded responses. that preserves data residency and minimizes cross-region chatter.
[02:20] Renee: on the unpinning drill — can you walk through the emergency unpin path if a new model version causes regressions?
[02:26] Priya: yeah so our standard unpin process is: detect via evals/telemetry -> autoswitch to pinned safe-version via version-gate -> if version-gate fails, we have a rollback runway which can be manual or automated. in the POC we set pins at the route level. an emergency unpin is an override that moves traffic off the bad version; we recommend a dry-run weekly to validate the orchestration.
[02:50] Mikael: can you be more concrete. like steps and timing, who clicks what in our console?
[02:55] Priya: sure. step 1 (0-2 min): telemetry alert from your monitors or our binding that quality threshold breached. step 2 (2-5 min): canary rollback policy triggered automatically to last-known-good. step 3 (5-10 min): if canary rollback not healthy, SE or ops can execute emergency unpin via the console 'force-unpin' control, which routes to the preapproved fallback variant. step 4 (10-30m): run a golden prompt smoke test. step 5: declare incident resolved and mark forensic logs. the dry-run next week will simulate that path with no real traffic.
[03:25] Diego: forensic logs — we need to ensure audit trails show which key and which tenant requested the unpin. our compliance needs that chain of custody.
[03:33] Jordan: yep, Redwood audit log entries include request id, operator id, and KMS key id if a key rotate occurred. we'll share an excerpt tonight.
[03:40] Mikael: are there any gotchas with KMS when you do model swaps? we manage keys in our cloud KMS.
[03:45] Priya: you can bring your own key (BYOK) and we integrate via our KMS connector. during a swap we don't re-encrypt model artifacts; we only reference the key for request-level encryption and payload encryption at rest. caveat: if you use on-prem HSM we have a slightly different flow and need a brief secure channel config.
[04:05] Renee: that aligns. Diego, any red flags on the security ask?
[04:09] Diego: i'd like to see a sample of the audit log JSON with an emergency unpin action, and confirmation that the key id is logged. also SAML/SSO flow for who can perform the force-unpin.
[04:20] Jordan: yes, action item — i'll include a redacted audit log sample and our RBAC matrix.
[04:25] Priya: back to performance — i want to flag the prefix cache hit ratio looked lower than expected on the sandbox, which is why p95 spiked. i suspect traffic pattern mismatch: your dataset has many unique prefixes. caching helps mostly on repeated system messages and common prompts.
[04:40] Mikael: hmm that might be a problem for classification workloads where every request is slightly different. what do you suggest?
[04:44] Priya: two levers: deterministic batching and smart prefix caching heuristics. deterministic batching groups similar seq-lengths to improve kernel efficiency. second, we can recommend small prompt rewrites to factor out noisy prefixes and move user-provided metadata into structured fields so the model sees consistent prefixes.
[05:04] Mikael: prompt rewrites are okay but we need product-level approvals, it's not trivial.
[05:08] Priya: understood. we can prototype a prompt-normalizer as an intermediate step in your pipeline — low-effort server-side change.
[05:15] Renee: can that normalizer run in our VPC? data residency again.
[05:18] Jordan: yes we can deploy a tiny function in your VPC or you can run our open-source normalizer.
[05:24] Diego: circling back to unpin drill — i'd like to run an afternoon tabletop where we simulate a model regression and everyone practices the flow. are you available next thursday?
[05:33] Jordan: yes we suggested 2026-08-27 in the next steps, works for our side.
[05:36] Mikael: one more thing on rollback: what's the visibility into the rollback percent? can we roll back 30% first?
[05:42] Priya: yes canary percentages are configurable. we recommend 10-25% initial canary depending on traffic; you can use linear ramp or instantaneous cutoff.
[05:52] Renee: for the POC, let's start with 10% canary for unpin and then 100% if green.
[05:58] Mikael: agreed. also we need to capture gating criteria — if accuracy on golden set drops by >2% then auto-cut.
[06:06] Priya: noted. i'll codify that as a telemetry rule in the runbook.
[06:10] Jordan: folks, any blockers on the cost side? we estimated burst dedicated will add about 12% over baseline in worst case.
[06:18] Mikael: budget is flexible for reliability but would like clear cost alerts.
[06:22] Jordan: we'll add cost burn alerts tied to burst utilization.
[06:27] Diego: quick question — competitor fallback. if you run out of capacity and you need to route to a third-party like OpenAI, is that an option?
[06:35] Jordan: we can configure third-party fallbacks but it's a last resort and has to be explicitly approved due to data residency and contract. for QuantaBank we recommend avoiding cross-provider fallback.
[06:45] Mikael: yep we won't allow external fallback.
[06:48] Priya: final note — we found a small regression in the 7b-q4 on one prompt type in the sandbox; the scorer flagged a 1.8% drop, close to your 2% threshold. we're going to run a targeted sweep tonight.
[06:59] Mikael: thanks, please send the sweep results and the raw evals.
[07:03] Jordan: will do. any other questions?
[07:06] Renee: just to confirm the tabletop next week will be a dry-run with no live traffic?
[07:10] Priya: correct, isolated test traffic only.
[07:13] Diego: and you'll send the audit log example, right?
[07:15] Jordan: yes, action item.
[07:17] Mikael: okay great — recap and next steps?
[07:20] Jordan: recap: priya runs 1k token shadow test and targeted sweep (due 26th), jordan sends security brief, audit log snippet and sandbox spreadsheet (due 24th), mikael provides golden prompt set and acceptance thresholds (due 25th), schedule tabletop 2026-08-27.
[07:36] Priya: thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript
